title: A coverage control whose population is derived the same way as its assertion cannot witness what the derivation misses -- classify against the widest possible population, not against the assertion's own narrower pattern
decided_by: BA + DBA + SecOps, ratified during #53's Phase 2/4 rounds (issue #53, merged to main as 055038e, PR #79)
content:
Standalone rule, generalising past voice-lint.mjs and gate-phase-entry.mjs's phase derivations. When an assertion CLAIMS a population by pattern-matching a source text, and its own anti-vacuity control ALSO derives that population by the same pattern (or a pattern of the same shape), the control cannot detect a case the pattern structurally cannot see. It will report 'found N, all accounted for' with total honesty, while the subject the assertion is supposed to police contains an N+1th member the pattern never had a chance to match. Green, honest, and blind, simultaneously. This is not a bug in the control's logic; it is a category error in what the control is FOR -- an anti-vacuity check answers 'is the population I derived non-empty and accounted for', never 'is the population I derived the RIGHT population'.

ORIGIN, #53. Two Lane-1 test suites (test-voice-lint.sh, test-gate-phase-entry-drift.sh) derived pipeline.md's current_phase literals with a regex matching only the unquoted-key assignment form (`current_phase: "..."`). pipeline.md writes one assignment, `"current_phase": "0-setup"`, in JSON-key form -- the single exception among 28 assignment occurrences. Both suites' 'every phase we found is accounted for' control was therefore blind to 0-setup by construction: the assertion's population and the control's population were the SAME narrowed set, so a phase absent from that set was not detected as unaccounted, it was never a candidate for accounting at all. Verified at HEAD c04b47c: both suites green (48/0 and 37/0) with the defect live, and the voice-lint control printed `found 26` (later corrected to the true 26-member count including 0-setup) as an honest report of the WRONG population, presented as reassurance.

THE FIX, generalised: replace 'assert every occurrence my narrow pattern matched is accounted for' with a TRI-PARTITION over the WIDEST population nothing can escape (in #53's case, every occurrence of the bare word `current_phase`, which no assignment spelling -- quoted, unquoted, backtick-valued, newline-split, wide-gapped -- can avoid containing). Every occurrence of that wide population must land in exactly one of: CLAIMED (matched by the narrow, shipped pattern), EXCLUDED-BY-A-STATED-RULE (matched by nothing, and the rule for why is stated and its membership asserted, not merely its count), or UNCLASSIFIED (matched by neither the shipped pattern nor the exclusion rule -- a real occurrence the derivation missed). UNCLASSIFIED must be asserted EMPTY. The EXCLUDED bucket's rule must itself be the NEGATION of a pattern STRICTLY WIDER than the claim pattern -- not an independently spelled third rule -- so the claim rule and the exclusion rule structurally cannot disagree about what counts as a match; two independently spelled rules can each fail to match the same real occurrence and let it fall silently into 'excluded' rather than surfacing in 'unclassified'. #53 measured this precisely: a naive same-line exclusion rule reported the real pipeline.md as 36 = 28 CLAIMED + 8 EXCLUDED + 0 UNCLASSIFIED, fully green, while a genuinely new assignment written across a line break (`current_phase\n  : "9-ghost"`) landed silently in EXCLUDED -- the bypass moved one level up, inside the fix meant to close it, with the identical shape (assertion and control sharing a blind spot) reproduced at a new coordinate.

THE RECURSIVE WARNING, worth stating explicitly because #53 hit it twice building its own fix: the FORM-COVERAGE CONTROL ITSELF IS SUBJECT TO THIS RULE. #53's round-0 form-coverage control used a permissive regex ANCHOR as its population and reported a population of 1 out of 8 real occurrences on a seven-assignment-form test fixture, printing `UNCLAIMED = 0`, GREEN -- byte-for-byte the same defect, one level up, inside #53's own fix for the defect. And the EXCLUDED bucket, once tri-partitioned correctly, was STILL pinned by a bare exact-count (`size == 8`) rather than by asserted membership in round 1 of the fix -- the same #33 shape-ratchet violation the CLAIMED side had already been corrected to avoid, in the SAME criterion, discovered independently by two reviewers. There is no fixed point at which 'the control is now wide enough' can be asserted from reading alone; it must be MEASURED against a fixture engineered to contain the classes the current pattern cannot see, and the population claimed by the control's own report must be justified independently of the pattern that produces it (count the bare word, not the assignment).

APPLY THIS TEST before shipping any 'we found everything, and here is proof we found everything' control: does the control's own population come from a DIFFERENT, WIDER derivation than the assertion it is meant to police? If the control's population is computed by narrowing (or by the same narrowing as) the assertion's own pattern, the control can only ever confirm the assertion is internally consistent with itself -- never that it is complete against its actual subject. See knowledge/living-context/architecture--phase-entry-0setup-prelude-declaration.json for the shipped mechanism and knowledge/living-context/architecture--status-schema-json-consumers.json for the four-copy phase-vocabulary catalog this issue widened two members of.
